findings.description: standard-cell power/ground pin 'VNB' reaches 17 distinct nets across 1196 instance(s) -- 'VDD' (2 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_22); 'VSS' (1097 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__a21o_1_0); 'addr[5]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_1_0); 'addr[6]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_1_1); 'clk' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_1_2); 'dout[12]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_25); 'dout[17]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_24); 'dout[23]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_27); 'dout[25]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_5); 'dout[26]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_29); 'dout[29]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_28); 'dout[5]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_17); 'ready' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_0); 'rst_n' (82 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__dfrtp_1_0); 'sa_q[0]' (2 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_10); 'sa_q[22]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_11); 'sa_q[6]' (1 instance(s), e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd__mux2_4_9). A single-power-domain block must wire every instance's same-named supply pin to the same net; declare options.power_connectivity.expected_nets to state which one is correct, or set options.power_connectivity: false if this design is genuinely multi-domain. If this design has no power distribution network routed at all -- every instance's supply pin landing on its own net is the same signature as no PDN having been added -- the more likely fix is request.power in klt place-and-route rather than either option above. Caveat for this ground pin: substrate continuity through the cells' own taps is not modelled in abstract-cell extraction, so separate Metal1 ground rails that a transistor-level extraction joins through the substrate are reported here as distinct nets -- this finding may be an artifact. To classify it, re-run klt extract without --abstract-cells and compare the pin's net count

153 top-level pin name(s) declared on both sides were anchored by name before comparing (options.anchor_top_level_pins): each one's layout net is asserted to match the reference net of the same-named pin, which the comparer's own topology-only net pairing does not otherwise require. Without it, two boundary nets with identical topology (e.g. two bits of a black-box macro's bus) are interchangeable and a swap between them compares clean -- see docs/cli/lvs.md, "Top-level pin anchoring"
